# A cyclic coordinate system for the class-number-seven theta calculation

## Result

Let K = Q(sqrt(-71)), omega = (1 + sqrt(-71))/2, and
O_m = Z + 29^m O_K. For every m >= 1,

**Pic(O_m) is cyclic of order 196 * 29^(m-1), generated by the proper
invertible ideal obtained by contracting a = (2, omega).**

This is an elementary mathematical deduction from the exact ideal-class
sequence and the finite residues checked by `ring_class_projection.py`.
It has not been formalized or checked in Lean. The script supplies exact
finite arithmetic, an implementation of the resulting projection, and
checks for the two concrete implementation risks described below.

No theta coefficients or new BSD theorem are claimed by this component.

## Proof and the finite certificate

1. Enumerating primitive reduced positive definite binary quadratic forms
   of discriminant -71 gives seven forms. Thus h_K = 7. The ideal a above
   2 is nonprincipal: a generator would have norm 2, but
   N(x+y omega) = (x+y/2)^2 + 71 y^2/4 cannot equal2. If y != 0 the second
   term already exceeds2; if y=0, x^2 cannot equal2. Hence [a] has order 7.

2. Put alpha = 10+omega. Its norm is128. At the prime (2,omega), alpha
   vanishes, while at the conjugate prime (2,omega-1), alpha is1 modulo2.
   Unique factorization of ideals therefore gives a^7 = (alpha). One can
   also check the multiplication matrix of alpha on the basis 1,omega:
   [[10,-18],[1,11]], whose determinant is128.

3. Since29 splits inK, the kernel in the usual ring-class exact sequence is

   (O_K/29^m O_K)^* / (Z/29^m Z)^* = (Z/29^m Z)^*.

   There is no additional unit quotient: O_K^*={+1,-1}, both diagonal.
   In this identification an element maps to the ratio of its two local
   values; choosing inverse reciprocity reverses that ratio and changes
   no order in this argument.

4. The roots of X^2-X+18 modulo 29 are 13 and 17. They lift to 477 and 365
   modulo 841. Thus the local ratio of alpha is

   rho = (10+477)/(10+365) = 322 (mod841).

   Its reduction is 3 modulo 29, of exact order 28, and

   rho^28 = 610 = 1 + 21*29 (mod841).

   Consequently v_29(rho^28-1)=1 in Z_29. The binomial lifting identity
   v_29((1+29u)^(29^r)-1)=r+1 for u a unit proves that the order of rho
   modulo 29^m is exactly 28*29^(m-1), for every m>=1.

5. Let a_m be the contracted ideal in O_m. If a_m^k is principal, extending
   to O_K shows7 dividesk. Write k=7d. The extended principal ideal has
   generator alpha^d, unique up to+/-1. It descends to a principal
   O_m-ideal precisely when alpha^d is a scalar unit modulo 29^m; equivalently
   rho^d=1. (The ideals and alpha are prime to the conductor, so extension
   and contraction give the standard bijection for these ideals.) The
   least positive d is therefore28*29^(m-1), and the order of a_m is
   196*29^(m-1).

6. The ring-class exact sequence gives the same order for the entire group:
   h(O_m)=7*29^m*(1-1/29)=196*29^(m-1). The elementa_m therefore generates it.
   Natural transition maps preserve this generator, making the coordinates
   compatible throughout the tower.

The class-group/form correspondence, invertible-ideal exact sequence, and
29-adic unit-lifting fact are the mathematical inputs. The script checks
their finite arithmetic premises; it does not prove those background
theorems by execution.

### Explicit ordinary-class coordinates

Reduction of the ideals a^j gives this ordered list, rather than an unordered
list of the seven classes:

| j | Reduced form for a^j |
|---|---|
| 0 | (1,1,18) |
| 1 | (2,-1,9) |
| 2 | (4,3,5) |
| 3 | (3,-1,6) |
| 4 | (3,1,6) |
| 5 | (4,-3,5) |
| 6 | (2,1,9) |

The script obtains these by lifting the root omega=0 modulo powers of 2,
forming the ideal (2^j,omega-r), and reducing the associated form. It also
checks that a^7 returns the principal class. The prime (29,omega-13) has
class a^4, while (29,omega-17) has class a^3. In particular neither is
principal. These coordinates also index the seven Gross-point values for
the auxiliary character calculation in `../logic/`.

There is also an independent factorization certificate: beta=7+3 omega has
norm 232=8*29, is divisible by the conjugate prime above2, and vanishes at
omega=17 modulo 29. Hence (beta)=conjugate(a)^3 * p17, giving [p17]=[a]^3
and [p13]=[a]^4 without relying on the reduction algorithm.

For example, if psi(a)=zeta_7 and chi=psi^2, then chi((29,omega-13))=zeta_7,
which is not 1. This is the unramified auxiliary character, distinct from
the trivial-tame projection below. At29, its values lie in Q_29 because
7 divides 28.

## How to use the result in the theta generator

Use the conductor exponent m and set W=29^(m-1). Enumerate every group element
as a_m^i for 0<=i<196W. Let c_i be its **correctly regularized, normalized**
Gross-point coefficient. Projection to the trivial finite-torsion character
then gives

    q_j = sum(c_(j+tW) for t in range(196)),  0 <= j < W.

Here the coordinate of the quotient generator is the image ofa_m. This
pushforward sums the 196 entries in each fiber. It does not divide by 196.
If downstream code instead chooses a_m^196 as its wild generator, its
coordinate is j*196^(-1) modulo W. The two coordinates must not be mixed.

`project_cycle()` accepts a complete ordered stream, uses O(W) memory, and
checks that exactly 196W coefficients were supplied. It cannot determine
whether a producer supplied the correct Gross point, quaternion embedding,
eigenvector value, orientation, or regularization at any index. Those must
be certified separately. Its synthetic fixture is explicitly not a theta
computation.

The tame and wild components of an element can also be recovered by the
CRT idempotents e_wild = 196 * 196^(-1) mod W and e_tame=1-e_wild modulo 196W.
The script checks those identities and includes the exponents in its output.

### Why a naive product can fail

Already at m=1, the group is C196. It is not C7 x C28: every element of
the latter has order dividing28. The order-seven Hilbert-class lift has a
nontrivial relation with the local 28-part. The cyclic coordinates remove
the need to select seven mutually compatible lifts and track that relation
by hand.

Keeping only the principal Hilbert class is also incorrect. The synthetic
fixture puts +1 at exponent 0 and -1 at exponent W. The full tame projection
is zero, but restricting to exponents divisible by 7 retains only +1, producing
a false nonvanishing result. This is a precise failure mode, not evidence
that the actual theta values have this pattern.

### Precision and conductor indexing

The wild quotient at conductor 29^m has order 29^(m-1), not 29^m. A coefficient
calculation modulo 29^k through degree 1<=d<29 descends from this finite quotient
only if m-1>=k. Otherwise ((1+T)^(29^(m-1))-1) can alter those coefficients.

For the quadratic coefficient modulo 841, use at least m=3:

| m | conductor | full group order | wild quotient order |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 29 | 196 | 1 |
| 2 | 841 | 5,684 | 29 |
| 3 | 24,389 | 164,836 | 841 |
| 4 | 707,281 | 4,780,244 | 24,389 |

The cheaper first attempt is modulo 29, at m=2: only 5,684 full-group values.
If the quadratic coefficient is nonzero modulo 29, it is already nonzero
29-adically and no higher precision is needed. If it is zero modulo 29,
that is inconclusive; escalate to m=3 and modulo 841. A zero residue must
not be treated as exact vanishing. This first attempt reduces the initial
orbit size by a factor of 29 compared with starting at precision841.

At m=2, the relation has linear coefficient 29 and quadratic coefficient 406,
both nonzero modulo 841. At m=3 both are zero modulo 841. The provided gate
checks the relevant binomial coefficients directly. It does not infer exact
vanishing of the constant or linear coefficient from finite residues; the
analytic interpolation and functional equation must supply those zeros.

## Interface to published definitions

Chida--Hsieh, *Special values of anticyclotomic L-functions for modular
forms*, Sections 4.2--4.3, define the group-ring theta element and then its
finite-character branch by this pushforward. See Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2,
and the definition preceding Theorem 4.6 in the author PDF:

https://www.math.ntu.edu.tw/~mlhsieh/research/central.pdf

This trivial finite branch is distinct from the auxiliary character used
to construct a generalized Kato class. See the literature and logic notes.
There is also an unresolved indexing/regularization dictionary between
the printed Castella--Hsieh numerical appendix and the general construction;
the projection here is valid independently of which producer is chosen,
but does not resolve that dictionary.

## Reproduce

    python projection/ring_class_projection.py --output projection/result.json

Run from `research/bsd-localization/`. Standard Python 3 only.
